# Geolonia Maps Documentation

> Official documentation for Geolonia Maps, a family of libraries for putting maps into websites and applications. All of them are built on MapLibre GL JS.

Geolonia Maps offers three libraries on top of a shared core. `embed` needs only a `<script>` tag and a `<div>` with `data-*` attributes. `maps-suite` drives the map imperatively from JavaScript. `maps-react` exposes the map as React components. All three sit on `@geolonia/maps-core`, whose `GeoloniaMap` class extends the MapLibre GL JS `Map`.

The site content is written in Japanese. This file is an English rendering of it. Code samples are reproduced verbatim, so string literals that are part of the sample data remain in Japanese.

Code samples use the demo key `YOUR-API-KEY`, which renders maps only on approved hosts such as `localhost`, GitHub Pages, CodePen, Netlify, Vercel and Cloudflare Pages. Publishing on your own domain requires a real key from https://app.geolonia.com/.

The generated API reference is not reproduced here. See https://docs.geolonia.com/reference/ for it.

---

## Introduction

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/

Geolonia Maps is a library set that gives you access to the maps Geolonia provides.

### Start from one of three libraries

Geolonia Maps offers three libraries on top of the core technology, so that people arriving from very different backgrounds can all use it. The tutorials provide three separate routes, one per library, so you can pick the one that matches your environment or the framework you already use.

Every page that shows code has tabs above the sample, letting you read the same map through the embed, maps-suite and maps-react lenses.

---

## Geolonia Maps Tutorials

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/

Let us build a practical map application with Geolonia Maps. By the end of the tutorials you will be able to display a map, change how it looks, put markers on it, and show your own data on it.

### Choosing the library that fits you

Geolonia Maps provides three libraries. They deliver the same capabilities in the way that suits each environment.

- **embed**: displays a map with nothing but a `<script>` tag and a `<div>` tag. This is the beginner-oriented library for "I just want a map".
- **maps-suite**: suited to migrating from another map service. Its API is designed so that existing users of such services find it easy to adopt.
- **maps-react**: the React-ready library. It handles dynamic switching of markers and data well.

All three are built on maps-core, which adapts MapLibre GL JS to Geolonia maps. That means that if you write TypeScript, every MapLibre GL JS feature remains available.

### Tutorial entry points

- embed: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/embed/
- maps-react: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/maps-react/
- maps-suite: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/maps-suite/

---

## embed Tutorial

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/embed/

embed is the easiest way to display a map in Geolonia Maps. It works by writing a `<div>` tag and a `<script>` tag into your HTML. No build tool and no npm required.

This tutorial climbs a ladder of capability from the bottom. Each rung is short and always produces something that works. By the top of rung 5 you will be able to publish a map carrying your own data at your own URL.

1. Rung 0, Show a Map: a map appears from a single HTML file
2. Rung 1, Place and Viewpoint: specify the place, the zoom level and the tilt
3. Rung 2, Add Data: overlay your own point data as GeoJSON
4. Rung 3, Change the Look: replace the base map style
5. Rung 4, Add Interaction: show a popup on click
6. Rung 5, Publish: obtain an API key and go to production

Every rung includes a "when it does not work" checklist.

---

## embed Rung 0: Show a Map

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/embed/first-map/

embed aims at the simplest possible map display. In this rung you create one HTML file and get a map into the browser.

### Displaying a map

Save the following as `index.html`.

```html
<!doctype html>
<html>
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <title>embed</title>
    <style>
      .geolonia { width: 100%; height: 400px; }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <div class="geolonia"></div>
    <script src="https://cdn.geolonia.com/embed/v5/embed?geolonia-api-key=YOUR-API-KEY"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

There are only two mechanisms at work.

- **A `div` carrying `class="geolonia"`**: this becomes the map. The `div` has no size of its own, so CSS gives it a height. A height of 0 means an invisible map.
- **The CDN `<script>`**: once loaded it looks for `.geolonia` elements on the page and turns them into maps. The `YOUR-API-KEY` in the URL is the trial demo key, which renders on development and preview environments such as `localhost`, GitHub Pages and CodePen. Issuing your own key happens at rung 5.

### Opening it in a browser

**Double-clicking the saved `index.html` will not show a map.** The demo key only renders for approved environments, and opening the file directly (`file://`) is not one of them.

The easy route is to start a simple local server in the folder holding `index.html` and open it as `localhost`.

```
# Node.js があるなら
npx serve

# Python があるなら
python3 -m http.server

# Windows で Python があるなら
py -m http.server
```

`npx serve` prints a URL on start. For `http.server`, open `http://localhost:8000/`.

If you already have a web server publishing HTML, uploading `index.html` there also works. Since the demo key only renders on approved environments, in that case go to rung 5 first, issue your own key and swap it in.

To try it without setting up a server at all, pasting into an online editor such as CodePen or JSFiddle also shows a map.

### Checking that it works

Since no place is specified, the map shows the whole world. If you can drag with the mouse and zoom with the wheel, it works.

**When it does not work**

- Blank white, nothing shown: check whether `.geolonia` has a **height of 0**.
- A message like "the map cannot be displayed": you are on an environment where the demo key does not apply. Check whether you opened the file directly (`file://`) and reopen it by the method above.
- Nothing happens at all: check the spelling of the `<script>` URL. It also fails offline.

**The attributes you can write**

Place and appearance come from `data-*` attributes on the `div`, introduced one at a time over the following rungs. The full list with defaults is the `EmbedAttributes` type in the reference: https://docs.geolonia.com/reference/embed/TypeAlias.EmbedAttributes/

---

## embed Rung 1: Place and Viewpoint

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/embed/view/

### Specifying place and zoom

Every embed setting is written as a **`data-*` attribute** on the `div`. Place is `data-lat` (latitude) and `data-lng` (longitude); zoom is `data-zoom`.

```html
<div class="geolonia"
     data-lat="35.658581" data-lng="139.745438" data-zoom="16"></div>
```

- **`data-lat` / `data-lng`**: latitude and longitude of the map centre. The values above are Tokyo Tower. You can get coordinates for your own place by right-clicking in Google Maps.
- **`data-zoom`**: zoom level. Larger numbers mean closer. As a rule of thumb, **11** shows a whole city, **14** a district, and **16** individual buildings.

### Tilting and rotating the viewpoint

`data-pitch` (tilt) and `data-bearing` (rotation) change the viewpoint itself.

```html
<style>
  .geolonia { width: 100%; height: 100vh; }
</style>

<div class="geolonia"
     data-lat="35.658581" data-lng="139.745438" data-zoom="16"
     data-pitch="45" data-bearing="20"></div>

<script src="https://cdn.geolonia.com/embed/v5/embed?geolonia-api-key=YOUR-API-KEY"></script>
```

- **`data-pitch`**: degrees by which the map tips towards the viewer. `0` is a flat top-down view.
- **`data-bearing`**: degrees by which the map rotates. `0` puts north at the top.

**When it does not work**

- The centre jumps to the sea or another country: you have **swapped latitude and longitude**. Within Japan, `data-lat` runs roughly 24 to 46 and `data-lng` roughly 123 to 146.
- An attribute has no effect: check its spelling. Unknown attributes are silently ignored. Write bare numbers only, with no unit or degree sign.

---

## embed Rung 2: Add Data

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/embed/data/

### Getting to know GeoJSON

To put data on the map with embed you use a file in the **GeoJSON** format, the standard format for geographic data. It is JSON, so a text editor is enough to read and write it.

```json
{
  "type": "FeatureCollection",
  "features": [
    {
      "type": "Feature",
      "geometry": { "type": "Point", "coordinates": [139.767125, 35.681236] },
      "properties": { "name": "東京駅" }
    }
  ]
}
```

- **`FeatureCollection`**: the container for features.
- **`geometry`**: the shape, such as point, line or polygon. `coordinates` is in **`[longitude, latitude]`** order, the reverse of `data-lat` and `data-lng`.
- **`properties`**: any attributes you want to attach, such as a name or a category.

### Overlaying data on the map

Put the GeoJSON file on a web server and add a `data-geojson` attribute to the `div`.

```html
<div class="geolonia"
     data-lat="35.68" data-lng="139.75" data-zoom="11"
     data-marker="off"
     data-geojson="/data/sample-spots.geojson"></div>
```

- **`data-geojson`**: the URL of the GeoJSON file. Either a path on the same server or an external URL that allows CORS.
- **`data-marker="off"`**: hides the centre marker. Turning it off is the usual move when you want to look at your data points.

### Making it readable with clustering

Once you have tens or hundreds of points they overlap and become unreadable. Adding `data-cluster="on"` groups nearby points automatically.

```html
<style>
  .geolonia { width: 100%; height: 100vh; }
</style>

<div class="geolonia"
     data-lat="35.68" data-lng="139.75" data-zoom="11"
     data-marker="off"
     data-geojson="/data/sample-spots.geojson"
     data-cluster="on"></div>

<script src="https://cdn.geolonia.com/embed/v5/embed?geolonia-api-key=YOUR-API-KEY"></script>
```

Zooming out turns individual points into clusters. To change the colour, specify something like `data-cluster-color="#ff0000"`.

### Swapping in your own data

1. Prepare one row per point in a spreadsheet or CSV, with longitude and latitude columns.
2. Convert it to GeoJSON. Writing it by hand works, and tools such as geojson.io make it easier. Geolonia also offers GeoJSON Maker at https://geolonia.github.io/geojson-maker/.
3. Put the file on a web server and change the `data-geojson` path.

**When it does not work**

- Points land in the sea or on another continent: check the **coordinate order**. GeoJSON `coordinates` is `[longitude, latitude]`, the reverse of the HTML `data-lat` and `data-lng`.
- Nothing appears: check the GeoJSON response in the network tab of the browser developer tools. A 404 or a JSON syntax error is the usual cause.
- GeoJSON at an external URL will not load: that is a CORS restriction. Try putting the file on the same server first.

---

## embed Rung 3: Change the Look

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/embed/style/

### What a style is

Everything about how a map looks, such as road colours, text size and building fills, is decided by a **style**. Styles are defined as JSON files and specified by URL.

In embed, writing a URL in the `data-style` attribute replaces the whole base map.

```html
<style>
  .geolonia { width: 100%; height: 100vh; }
</style>

<div class="geolonia"
     data-lat="35.68" data-lng="139.75" data-zoom="11"
     data-marker="off"
     data-geojson="/data/sample-spots.geojson"
     data-style="https://tile.openstreetmap.jp/styles/osm-bright/style.json"></div>

<script src="https://cdn.geolonia.com/embed/v5/embed?geolonia-api-key=YOUR-API-KEY"></script>
```

- **`data-style`**: the URL of a style JSON. The example above is a style published by OpenStreetMap Japan.
- Omitting `data-style` uses the Geolonia standard style.

### Styles Geolonia provides

Geolonia Maps ships several styles. Writing the name in `data-style` is enough to switch.

```html
<div class="geolonia" data-style="geolonia/basic-v2"></div>
<div class="geolonia" data-style="geolonia/midnight"></div>
<div class="geolonia" data-style="geolonia/notebook"></div>
```

The list of usable style names is at https://docs.geolonia.com/explanation/styles/.

**When it does not work**

- The map turns blank white: check the spelling of the style URL. A URL that does not exist renders nothing.
- The GeoJSON data disappeared: check that you did not delete the `data-geojson` attribute. Style and data are independent settings and can both be specified at once.

---

## embed Rung 4: Add Interaction

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/embed/interaction/

### How popups work

In embed, HTML written inside the `.geolonia` div becomes **the popup of the marker**. A marker stands at the centre, and clicking it opens the content as a popup.

```html
<style>
  .geolonia { width: 100%; height: 100vh; }
</style>

<div class="geolonia" data-lat="35.681236" data-lng="139.767125" data-zoom="15">
  <strong>東京駅</strong><br>JR・地下鉄各線
</div>

<script src="https://cdn.geolonia.com/embed/v5/embed?geolonia-api-key=YOUR-API-KEY"></script>
```

There are two points to note.

- **The child elements of the `div`** become the popup content as they are. Being HTML, bold text and links work.
- Writing child elements automatically raises a marker at the centre, unless `data-marker="off"` is set.

### The limits of embed popups

An embed popup can only be attached to **the single centre marker**. Attaching a popup to each of several markers requires a JavaScript implementation, which means the maps-suite or maps-react tutorials.

One popup is still enough to answer "what is this place?". For a map embedded on a shop page, putting the address and opening hours in the popup makes it clear.

### Combining with GeoJSON

`data-geojson` from rung 2 and a popup (child elements) can be used together. Several data points appear, and a marker with a popup stands at the centre as well.

```html
<div class="geolonia"
     data-lat="35.68" data-lng="139.75" data-zoom="11"
     data-geojson="/data/sample-spots.geojson">
  <strong>東京の主要スポット</strong><br>5地点を表示しています
</div>
```

**When it does not work**

- No marker appears: check that `data-marker="off"` is not still present. Popups need a marker.
- The popup is empty: check that the child elements of the `div` are not empty. Whitespace alone will not open a popup.
- Child elements have no effect: watch for an unclosed `div` tag. Close it properly, as in `<div class="geolonia" ...>content</div>`.

---

## embed Rung 5: Publish

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/embed/publish/

### Demo key versus production key

Every code sample so far wrote `YOUR-API-KEY` in the CDN URL. That is a **demo key** prepared by Geolonia, and it works on development and preview environments such as `localhost`, GitHub Pages, CodePen, Netlify and Vercel.

Publishing on your own domain requires issuing a **production API key**.

### Obtaining an API key

1. Log in to the Geolonia dashboard at https://app.geolonia.com/.
2. Create a new key in the API key management screen.
3. Register **the domain you will use**, for example `example.com`. The map renders only on registered domains.

### Rewriting the code

Replace `YOUR-API-KEY` with the key you obtained. Nothing else changes.

```html
<!doctype html>
<html>
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <title>My Map</title>
    <style>
      .geolonia { width: 100%; height: 400px; }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <div class="geolonia"
         data-lat="35.68" data-lng="139.75" data-zoom="11"
         data-marker="off"
         data-geojson="/data/sample-spots.geojson"
         data-cluster="on">
    </div>
    <script src="https://cdn.geolonia.com/embed/v5/embed?geolonia-api-key=YOUR-REAL-API-KEY"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

### Publishing

embed runs from an HTML file alone, so there is no build step. Upload the file to static hosting as it is.

- **GitHub Pages**: put `index.html` in the repository and enable Pages.
- **Netlify or Vercel**: connect the repository, and that is all.
- **Shared hosting**: upload the file over FTP or similar.

Do not forget to put the GeoJSON file on the same server, somewhere the `data-geojson` path resolves.

**When it does not work**

- "The map cannot be displayed" appears: check that the domain registered on the API key matches the actual domain. `www.example.com` and `example.com` count as different domains.
- It worked locally but not on the server: check that the demo key (`YOUR-API-KEY`) has not been left in place.
- Only the GeoJSON fails: check that the file is deployed on the server and that the path is correct.

---

## maps-suite Tutorial

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/maps-suite/

maps-suite is the library for driving Geolonia Maps **imperatively from JavaScript**. Its class structure of `Map`, `Marker` and `InfoWindow` will look familiar to anyone who has used another map service, and it supports the straightforward "create a map, then call methods on it" style. It works in any web page regardless of framework.

By the top of rung 5 you will be able to publish, at your own URL, a map carrying your own data with colours driven by its attributes.

1. Rung 0, Show a Map: a map appears from `new geolonia.maps.Map()`
2. Rung 1, Place and Viewpoint: specify the place, the zoom level and the tilt
3. Rung 2, Add Data: overlay your own point data as GeoJSON
4. Rung 3, Change the Look: colour points by a data attribute
5. Rung 4, Add Interaction: open an info window on marker click
6. Rung 5, Publish: build and go to production

---

## maps-suite Rung 0: Show a Map

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/maps-suite/first-map/

Any build environment works. If you do not have one yet, the vanilla JavaScript template of Vite is the easy option.

### Installing

Install maps-suite together with maplibre-gl, the rendering engine.

```
npm install @geolonia/maps-suite maplibre-gl
```

### Displaying a map

First prepare an element in the HTML to hold the map. The element has no size of its own, so give it a height in CSS.

```html
<!doctype html>
<html>
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <title>suite</title>
    <style>
      #map { width: 100%; height: 100vh; }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <div id="map"></div>
    <script type="module" src="/main.js"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

Then import the CSS and create a `Map` in `main.js`.

```js
import "maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css";
import "@geolonia/maps-core/css";
import { geolonia } from "@geolonia/maps-suite";

new geolonia.maps.Map(document.getElementById("map"), {
  apiKey: "YOUR-API-KEY",
});
```

There are three points to note.

- **The CSS imports**: both `maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css` and `@geolonia/maps-core/css` are required. Forgetting them breaks the layout of controls and popups.
- **`new geolonia.maps.Map(element, options)`**: the first argument is **the HTML element itself**. Passing an id string such as `"map"` raises an exception.
- **`apiKey`**: `YOUR-API-KEY` is the trial demo key.

### Checking that it works

Start the dev server with `npm run dev` and open it in a browser. Without a centre, maps-suite shows **the whole world**, at latitude and longitude `0, 0` and zoom `0`.

**When it does not work**

- Blank white, nothing shown: check whether `#map` has a **height of 0**.
- An exception reading "The first argument must be an HTMLElement": you are passing an id **string** to `Map`. Retrieve the element with `document.getElementById("map")` and pass that.
- The layout breaks, for example control icons appear in odd places: **a missing CSS import**. Check that both are loaded.

---

## maps-suite Rung 1: Place and Viewpoint

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/maps-suite/view/

### Specifying place and zoom

Place and zoom are given as **options** when creating the `Map`. Place is `center` and zoom is `zoom`.

```js
const map = new geolonia.maps.Map(document.getElementById("map"), {
  apiKey: "YOUR-API-KEY",
  center: { lat: 35.658581, lng: 139.745438 },
  zoom: 16,
});
```

- **`center`**: the map centre, passed as a `{ lat, lng }` object. The values above are Tokyo Tower.
- **`zoom`**: zoom level. As a rule of thumb, **11** shows a whole city, **14** a district, and **16** individual buildings.

You can also move the map after creating it: `map.setCenter({ lat, lng })` to move, `map.panTo({ lat, lng })` for an animated move, and `map.setZoom(14)` to change the zoom.

### Tilting and rotating the viewpoint

Tilt and rotation are also `Map` options. maps-suite calls tilt `tilt` and rotation `heading`.

```js
import "maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css";
import "@geolonia/maps-core/css";
import { geolonia } from "@geolonia/maps-suite";

const map = new geolonia.maps.Map(document.getElementById("map"), {
  apiKey: "YOUR-API-KEY",
  center: { lat: 35.658581, lng: 139.745438 },
  zoom: 16,
  tilt: 45,     // 地図を手前に倒す角度（度）。0 が真上からの平面図
  heading: 20,  // 地図を回す角度（度）。0 が北が上
});
```

`tilt` is the angle by which the map tips towards the viewer and `heading` the angle by which it rotates, both in degrees. Both default to `0`, giving a flat top-down view with north at the top.

They can be changed afterwards too: `map.setTilt(45)` for tilt, `map.setHeading(20)` for rotation, and `map.moveCamera({ center, zoom, tilt, heading })` to move them together with centre and zoom. None of these require waiting for the map to load.

When you need an operation that only exists in maplibre, `map.getGeoloniaMap()` retrieves the underlying map instance. The next rung uses it for adding data.

**When it does not work**

- The centre jumps to the sea or another country: check for **swapped** `lat` and `lng`. Within Japan, `lat` runs roughly 24 to 46 and `lng` roughly 123 to 146.
- A "function does not exist" error from `setPitch` or `setBearing`: in maps-suite the names are `setTilt` and `setHeading`. `pitch` and `bearing` are the underlying maplibre names.
- Buildings became three-dimensional when you tilted: maps-suite enables 3D buildings by default. Pass `threeDimensional: false` to keep it flat.

---

## maps-suite Rung 2: Add Data

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/maps-suite/data/

### Getting to know GeoJSON

This tutorial uses a sample of five places in Tokyo. Save the following as `public/data/sample-spots.geojson`. With Vite, files under `public/` are served at URLs like `/data/...`.

```json
{
  "type": "FeatureCollection",
  "features": [
    { "type": "Feature", "geometry": { "type": "Point", "coordinates": [139.767125, 35.681236] }, "properties": { "name": "東京駅", "category": "ターミナル" } },
    { "type": "Feature", "geometry": { "type": "Point", "coordinates": [139.700258, 35.690921] }, "properties": { "name": "新宿駅", "category": "ターミナル" } },
    { "type": "Feature", "geometry": { "type": "Point", "coordinates": [139.701636, 35.658034] }, "properties": { "name": "渋谷駅", "category": "ターミナル" } },
    { "type": "Feature", "geometry": { "type": "Point", "coordinates": [139.796747, 35.714765] }, "properties": { "name": "浅草寺", "category": "観光" } },
    { "type": "Feature", "geometry": { "type": "Point", "coordinates": [139.745438, 35.658581] }, "properties": { "name": "東京タワー", "category": "観光" } }
  ]
}
```

The `category` values are `ターミナル` (terminal station) and `観光` (sightseeing); the next rung uses them.

- **`geometry`**: `coordinates` is in **`[longitude, latitude]`** order, the reverse of the `{ lat, lng }` used by `center`.
- **`properties`**: attributes attached to the feature. Here `name` and `category`.

### Overlaying data on the map

Adding data uses `getGeoloniaMap()`, mentioned by name in rung 1. It is **the public API for touching the underlying maplibre map directly**, and it is where you go for anything maps-suite does not provide. You register a source (the data) and stack a layer (how to draw it) on top.

There is also a shorter form, `map.data`, for simply loading GeoJSON, but this rung wants control over the drawing, so source and layer are handled separately.

```js
import "maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css";
import "@geolonia/maps-core/css";
import { geolonia } from "@geolonia/maps-suite";

const map = new geolonia.maps.Map(document.getElementById("map"), {
  apiKey: "YOUR-API-KEY",
  center: { lat: 35.68, lng: 139.75 },
  zoom: 11,
});

await map.whenReady();
const impl = map.getGeoloniaMap();
impl.addSource("spots", { type: "geojson", data: "/data/sample-spots.geojson" });
impl.addLayer({ id: "spots", type: "circle", source: "spots" });
```

- **`addSource`**: registers the data supply. With `type: "geojson"`, `data` takes a URL or the object itself.
- **`addLayer`**: stacks a way of drawing the data. `type: "circle"` draws each point as a circle. `source` names the registered source.
- **Order matters**: the source referenced by `addLayer` must be added first, and both must be called after the map has finished loading, which `whenReady()` waits for.

**When it does not work**

- An error such as "Style is not done loading": you called `addSource` or `addLayer` **without waiting** for `whenReady()`. Check the `await`.
- Points land in the sea or on another continent: **longitude and latitude are reversed** in the GeoJSON `coordinates`. Put them in `[longitude, latitude]` order.
- Nothing appears but there is no error: check the GeoJSON response in the network tab. A 404 or a JSON syntax error is the usual cause.

---

## maps-suite Rung 3: Change the Look

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/maps-suite/style/

### Deciding how to draw with paint properties

The **`paint`** entry of the layer definition passed to `addLayer` controls the drawing in detail.

```js
impl.addLayer({
  id: "spots",
  type: "circle",
  source: "spots",
  paint: {
    "circle-radius": 8,
    "circle-stroke-width": 2,
    "circle-stroke-color": "#fff",
    "circle-color": "#e4402f",
  },
});
```

- **`circle-radius`**: circle radius in pixels.
- **`circle-stroke-width` and `circle-stroke-color`**: outline width and colour. A white outline makes points readable over the map.
- **`circle-color`**: fill colour.

### Varying colour by data attribute

`circle-color` accepts not only a fixed colour but also an **expression**. A `match` expression builds a lookup table saying "if `category` has this value, use this colour".

```js
import "maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css";
import "@geolonia/maps-core/css";
import { geolonia } from "@geolonia/maps-suite";

const map = new geolonia.maps.Map(document.getElementById("map"), {
  apiKey: "YOUR-API-KEY",
  center: { lat: 35.68, lng: 139.75 },
  zoom: 11,
});

await map.whenReady();
const impl = map.getGeoloniaMap();
impl.addSource("spots", { type: "geojson", data: "/data/sample-spots.geojson" });
impl.addLayer({
  id: "spots",
  type: "circle",
  source: "spots",
  paint: {
    "circle-radius": 8,
    "circle-stroke-width": 2,
    "circle-stroke-color": "#fff",
    "circle-color": [
      "match",
      ["get", "category"],
      "ターミナル", "#e4402f",
      "観光", "#2b6cb0",
      "#888888",
    ],
  },
});
```

Reading the array from the top:

1. `"match"`: the expression that looks up a table.
2. `["get", "category"]`: takes the `properties.category` value of each point.
3. `"ターミナル", "#e4402f"`: red if the value is "terminal".
4. `"観光", "#2b6cb0"`: blue if the value is "sightseeing".
5. `"#888888"`: the colour when nothing matches. This fallback is **required**.

Deciding appearance from data attributes like this is called **data-driven styling**. Beyond colour, you can vary `circle-radius` by value, drawing larger circles for larger numbers.

### Changing the base map itself

To change the appearance of the background map rather than the point colours, pass a style name or URL in the `style` option when creating the `Map`.

```js
const map = new geolonia.maps.Map(document.getElementById("map"), {
  apiKey: "YOUR-API-KEY",
  style: "geolonia/midnight",
});
```

**When it does not work**

- Everything takes the fallback colour: check that the values written in `match` **match exactly** the values in the GeoJSON `properties`. Watch for full-width versus half-width characters and stray whitespace.
- Nothing renders any more: **forgetting the fallback**, the last entry, makes the `match` expression invalid. Always put a default colour at the end.
- A misspelled property name produces no error and no effect. Watch for spellings such as `circle-colour`.

---

## maps-suite Rung 4: Add Interaction

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/maps-suite/interaction/

### Marker and InfoWindow

maps-suite has a `Marker` class for standing a pin at one point on the map and an `InfoWindow` class for showing a balloon. The assembly is to open the info window from the marker click event.

```js
import "maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css";
import "@geolonia/maps-core/css";
import { geolonia } from "@geolonia/maps-suite";

const map = new geolonia.maps.Map(document.getElementById("map"), {
  apiKey: "YOUR-API-KEY",
  center: { lat: 35.681236, lng: 139.767125 },
  zoom: 15,
});

const marker = new geolonia.maps.Marker({
  position: { lat: 35.681236, lng: 139.767125 },
  map,
  title: "東京駅",
});

const infoWindow = new geolonia.maps.InfoWindow({
  content: "<strong>東京駅</strong><br>JR・地下鉄各線",
});

marker.addListener("click", () => {
  infoWindow.open(map, marker);
});
```

- **`Marker`**: passing `position` (`{ lat, lng }`) and `map` raises a marker at that place. `title` is the hover tooltip. You can later remove it with `marker.setMap(null)` or move it with `setPosition`.
- **`InfoWindow`**: created with `content`, an HTML string or an HTML element. Nothing is shown at this point.
- **`marker.addListener("click", ...)`**: receives clicks on the marker.
- **`infoWindow.open(map, marker)`**: opens the info window at the position of the given marker. The arguments are **these two in this order**: map, then anchor.

### Receiving map clicks

Clicks on the map itself can also be received. The coordinates of the click are in `e.latLng`.

```js
map.addListener("click", (e) => {
  console.log("クリック位置:", e.latLng.lat(), e.latLng.lng());
});
```

To "put a marker where the user clicked", just call `new geolonia.maps.Marker({ position: e.latLng.toJSON(), map })` inside that handler. `toJSON()` converts to a plain `{ lat, lng }` object.

**When it does not work**

- No marker appears: check that you passed `map` in the `Marker` options. Without it the marker is created but never attached to a map.
- Clicking does not open it: check **the argument order** of `open(map, marker)`. The first argument is the map, the second the marker.
- The balloon is empty: check that `content` is not an empty string.

---

## maps-suite Rung 5: Publish

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/maps-suite/publish/

### Demo key versus production key

Every code sample so far wrote `apiKey: "YOUR-API-KEY"`, the demo key, which works on development and preview environments. Publishing on your own domain requires issuing a production API key.

### Obtaining an API key

1. Log in to the Geolonia dashboard at https://app.geolonia.com/.
2. Create a new key in the API key management screen.
3. Register the domain you will use. The map renders only on registered domains.

### Rewriting the code

```js
const map = new geolonia.maps.Map(document.getElementById("map"), {
  apiKey: "YOUR-REAL-API-KEY",
  center: { lat: 35.68, lng: 139.75 },
  zoom: 11,
});
```

The API key is a publishable key used for rendering maps, but setting a domain restriction prevents unauthorised use from other sites.

### Building and publishing

Building produces static files. With Vite:

```
npm run build
```

HTML, JS and CSS are emitted into `dist/`, and putting that on static hosting publishes it.

- **GitHub Pages**: deploy the contents of `dist/`, usually via Actions.
- **Netlify or Vercel**: connecting the repository detects the build command and deploys automatically.
- **Shared hosting**: upload the contents of `dist/` over FTP or similar.

GeoJSON placed in `public/data/` is copied to `dist/data/` by the build and published along with everything else.

**When it does not work**

- "The map cannot be displayed" appears: check that the domain registered on the API key matches the actual domain. `www.example.com` and `example.com` count as different domains.
- It worked locally but not in production: check that the demo key has not been left in place.
- Only the data fails: check that the GeoJSON URL resolves in production. Publishing under a subdirectory can break absolute paths such as `/data/...`; check the Vite `base` setting.

---

## maps-react Tutorial

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/maps-react/

maps-react is the library for using Geolonia Maps **as React components**. Putting `<Map>` in your JSX produces a map, and markers and data are declared through props and children. In a React site or application it works as it is under almost any build environment, including Vite, Next.js and webpack.

1. Rung 0, Show a Map: a map appears from a single `<Map>` component
2. Rung 1, Place and Viewpoint: specify place, zoom and tilt through props
3. Rung 2, Add Data: overlay your own point data as GeoJSON
4. Rung 3, Change the Look: colour points by a data attribute
5. Rung 4, Add Interaction: show a popup on click
6. Rung 5, Publish: build and go to production

---

## maps-react Rung 0: Show a Map

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/maps-react/first-map/

### Installing

Install maps-react together with maplibre-gl, the rendering engine. maplibre-gl is the same engine that underlies other React map libraries such as react-map-gl, and it is installed as a separate package.

```
npm install @geolonia/maps-react maplibre-gl
```

### Displaying a map

Import the `Map` component and the CSS the map needs, then put it in the JSX.

```jsx
import "maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css";
import "@geolonia/maps-core/css";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import { Map } from "@geolonia/maps-react";

createRoot(document.getElementById("root")).render(
  <Map
    apiKey="YOUR-API-KEY"
    containerStyle={{ width: "100%", height: "100vh" }}
  />,
);
```

There are three points to note.

- **The CSS imports**: both `maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css` and `@geolonia/maps-core/css` are required.
- **`containerStyle`**: the size of the element holding the map. A size of 0 means an invisible map, so always give it a height.
- **`apiKey`**: `YOUR-API-KEY` is the trial demo key.

### Checking that it works

Start the dev server with `npm run dev`. Since `center` is not specified, the first view is the maps-react default, a world map.

**When it does not work**

- Blank white, nothing shown: check whether `containerStyle` has a **height of 0**. The same applies if the parent element has `height: 0`.
- The layout breaks: **a missing CSS import**.
- The console shows `The requested module '.../maplibre-gl.js' does not provide an export named 'default'`: maplibre-gl is distributed in CJS form and some build environments do not pre-bundle it. In Vite-based environments such as Astro, adding `vite: { optimizeDeps: { include: ['maplibre-gl', '@geolonia/maps-core'] } }` to the config resolves it. A plain Vite SPA usually does not need this.

---

## maps-react Rung 1: Place and Viewpoint

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/maps-react/view/

### Specifying place and zoom

Every maps-react setting is written as a **prop** on the `Map` component. Place is `center` and zoom is `zoom`.

```jsx
<Map
  apiKey="YOUR-API-KEY"
  center={[139.745438, 35.658581]}
  zoom={16}
  containerStyle={{ width: "100%", height: "100vh" }}
/>
```

- **`center`**: the coordinates of the map centre, in **`[longitude, latitude]` order**. The values above are Tokyo Tower. Google Maps shows coordinates as "latitude, longitude", so swap them before use.
- **`zoom`**: zoom level. **11** shows a whole city, **14** a district, **16** individual buildings.

### Tilting and rotating the viewpoint

`pitch` (tilt) and `bearing` (rotation) change the viewpoint. The sample also raises a marker at the centre.

```jsx
import "maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css";
import "@geolonia/maps-core/css";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import { Map } from "@geolonia/maps-react";

createRoot(document.getElementById("root")).render(
  <Map
    apiKey="YOUR-API-KEY"
    center={[139.745438, 35.658581]}
    zoom={16}
    pitch={45}
    bearing={20}
    marker
    markerColor="#e4402f"
    containerStyle={{ width: "100%", height: "100vh" }}
  />,
);
```

- **`pitch`**: degrees by which the map tips towards the viewer. `0` is a flat top-down view.
- **`bearing`**: degrees by which the map rotates. `0` puts north at the top.
- **`marker` and `markerColor`**: whether to raise a marker at the centre, and its colour.

**When it does not work**

- The centre jumps to the sea or another country: you have **swapped longitude and latitude**. `center` is in `[longitude, latitude]` order. Within Japan, longitude runs roughly 123 to 146 and latitude roughly 24 to 46.
- A prop has no effect: check that you are not passing the value as a string. Write `zoom={16}` rather than `zoom="16"`; numbers and arrays go through the JSX braces.

---

## maps-react Rung 2: Add Data

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/maps-react/data/

### Getting to know GeoJSON

This tutorial uses the same five-place sample as the maps-suite track. Save it as `public/data/sample-spots.geojson`.

```json
{
  "type": "FeatureCollection",
  "features": [
    { "type": "Feature", "geometry": { "type": "Point", "coordinates": [139.767125, 35.681236] }, "properties": { "name": "東京駅", "category": "ターミナル" } },
    { "type": "Feature", "geometry": { "type": "Point", "coordinates": [139.700258, 35.690921] }, "properties": { "name": "新宿駅", "category": "ターミナル" } },
    { "type": "Feature", "geometry": { "type": "Point", "coordinates": [139.701636, 35.658034] }, "properties": { "name": "渋谷駅", "category": "ターミナル" } },
    { "type": "Feature", "geometry": { "type": "Point", "coordinates": [139.796747, 35.714765] }, "properties": { "name": "浅草寺", "category": "観光" } },
    { "type": "Feature", "geometry": { "type": "Point", "coordinates": [139.745438, 35.658581] }, "properties": { "name": "東京タワー", "category": "観光" } }
  ]
}
```

- **`geometry`**: `coordinates` is in **`[longitude, latitude]`** order, the same order as `center`.
- **`properties`**: here `name` and `category`.

### Overlaying data on the map

In maps-react, data is declared in JSX too. Put `Source` (the data) as a child of `Map`, and `Layer` (how to draw it) inside that.

```jsx
import "maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css";
import "@geolonia/maps-core/css";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import { Layer, Map, Source } from "@geolonia/maps-react";

createRoot(document.getElementById("root")).render(
  <Map
    apiKey="YOUR-API-KEY"
    center={[139.75, 35.68]}
    zoom={11}
    containerStyle={{ width: "100%", height: "100vh" }}
  >
    <Source id="spots" type="geojson" data="/data/sample-spots.geojson">
      <Layer id="spots" type="circle" />
    </Source>
  </Map>,
);
```

- **`<Source>`**: the data supply. With `type="geojson"`, `data` takes the GeoJSON URL or the object itself.
- **`<Layer>`**: how to draw the data. `type="circle"` draws each point as a circle. **`id` is required.** Omitting it adds no layer and raises no error, so nothing appears.

**When it does not work**

- Nothing appears and there is no error: **a missing `id` on `<Layer>`** is the most common cause.
- Points land in the sea or on another continent: **longitude and latitude are reversed** in `coordinates`.
- Still nothing: check the GeoJSON response in the network tab.

---

## maps-react Rung 3: Change the Look

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/maps-react/style/

### Deciding how to draw with paint properties

The **`paint`** prop of `<Layer>` controls the drawing in detail.

```jsx
<Layer
  id="spots"
  type="circle"
  paint={{
    "circle-radius": 8,
    "circle-stroke-width": 2,
    "circle-stroke-color": "#fff",
    "circle-color": "#e4402f",
  }}
/>
```

### Varying colour by data attribute

```jsx
import "maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css";
import "@geolonia/maps-core/css";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import { Layer, Map, Source } from "@geolonia/maps-react";

createRoot(document.getElementById("root")).render(
  <Map
    apiKey="YOUR-API-KEY"
    center={[139.75, 35.68]}
    zoom={11}
    containerStyle={{ width: "100%", height: "100vh" }}
  >
    <Source id="spots" type="geojson" data="/data/sample-spots.geojson">
      <Layer
        id="spots"
        type="circle"
        paint={{
          "circle-radius": 8,
          "circle-stroke-width": 2,
          "circle-stroke-color": "#fff",
          "circle-color": [
            "match",
            ["get", "category"],
            "ターミナル", "#e4402f",
            "観光", "#2b6cb0",
            "#888888",
          ],
        }}
      />
    </Source>
  </Map>,
);
```

Reading the array from the top:

1. `"match"`: the expression that looks up a table.
2. `["get", "category"]`: takes the `properties.category` value of each point.
3. `"ターミナル", "#e4402f"`: red if the value is "terminal".
4. `"観光", "#2b6cb0"`: blue if the value is "sightseeing".
5. `"#888888"`: the fallback colour, which is **required**.

### Changing the base map itself

Pass a style name or URL in the `style` prop of `Map`.

```jsx
<Map apiKey="YOUR-API-KEY" style="geolonia/midnight" ...>
```

**When it does not work**

- Everything takes the fallback colour: check that the values written in `match` **match exactly** the values in the GeoJSON `properties`.
- Nothing renders any more: **forgetting the fallback** makes the `match` expression invalid.
- A misspelled property name produces no error and no effect.

---

## maps-react Rung 4: Add Interaction

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/maps-react/interaction/

### The Marker component

maps-react has a `Marker` component for standing a pin at one point. Put it as a child of `Map` and give the place with `lat` and `lng`. What makes it feel like React is that **the children of `Marker` become the popup content**.

```jsx
import "maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css";
import "@geolonia/maps-core/css";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import { Map, Marker } from "@geolonia/maps-react";

createRoot(document.getElementById("root")).render(
  <Map
    apiKey="YOUR-API-KEY"
    center={[139.767125, 35.681236]}
    zoom={15}
    containerStyle={{ width: "100%", height: "100vh" }}
  >
    <Marker lat={35.681236} lng={139.767125} color="#e4402f">
      <strong>東京駅</strong>
      <p style={{ margin: 0 }}>JR・地下鉄各線</p>
    </Marker>
  </Map>,
);
```

- **`lat` and `lng`**: where the marker stands. Unlike `center`, which is a `[longitude, latitude]` array, these are **separate props**.
- **`color`**: the marker colour.
- **Children**: the popup content opened on click. Being JSX, React components can go in it too.

### Building several markers from data

`Marker` is an ordinary React component, so mapping over an array produces data-driven markers.

```jsx
const spots = [
  { name: "東京駅", lat: 35.681236, lng: 139.767125 },
  { name: "新宿駅", lat: 35.690921, lng: 139.700258 },
  { name: "渋谷駅", lat: 35.658034, lng: 139.701636 },
];

<Map apiKey="YOUR-API-KEY" center={[139.73, 35.68]} zoom={12}
     containerStyle={{ width: "100%", height: "100vh" }}>
  {spots.map((s) => (
    <Marker key={s.name} lat={s.lat} lng={s.lng}>
      <strong>{s.name}</strong>
    </Marker>
  ))}
</Map>
```

Combined with state, a UI where "clicking a list entry adds a marker to the map" needs nothing beyond ordinary React.

**When it does not work**

- A marker appears in an odd place: check for **swapped** `lat` and `lng`. `center` is a `[longitude, latitude]` array, but `Marker` takes named `lat=` and `lng=` props.
- The popup does not open: check that the children are not empty. A `Marker` with no children is a marker with no popup.
- A warning about multiple markers: remember `key` when building from an array, as in ordinary React.

---

## maps-react Rung 5: Publish

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/tutorials/maps-react/publish/

### Demo key versus production key

Every code sample so far wrote `apiKey="YOUR-API-KEY"`, the demo key. Publishing on your own domain requires issuing a production API key from https://app.geolonia.com/ and registering the domain.

```jsx
<Map
  apiKey="YOUR-REAL-API-KEY"
  center={[139.75, 35.68]}
  zoom={11}
  containerStyle={{ width: "100%", height: "100vh" }}
>
  ...
</Map>
```

### Building and publishing

A React application becomes static files when built. With Vite:

```
npm run build
```

HTML, JS and CSS are emitted into `dist/`, and putting that on static hosting publishes it. GeoJSON placed in `public/data/` is copied to `dist/data/` by the build.

**When it does not work**

- "The map cannot be displayed" appears: check that the registered domain matches the actual domain.
- It worked locally but not in production: check that the demo key has not been left in place.
- Only the data fails: check that the GeoJSON URL resolves in production, and check the Vite `base` setting if you published under a subdirectory.

## Place Multiple Markers

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/howto/multiple-markers/

Put several places on the map at once. One point is served well enough by the centre marker, but **two or more calls for a list plus a loop**. Hold coordinates in `[longitude, latitude]` order.

### embed

embed, using HTML attributes alone, has **no** declarative way to place multiple markers. The only marker it can embed is the single centre one. To show several points, either turn the points into GeoJSON and load them with `data-geojson`, or switch to the maps-suite or maps-react code.

### maps-suite

Loop over the list and create a `Marker` for each.

```js
import "maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css";
import "@geolonia/maps-core/css";
import { geolonia } from "@geolonia/maps-suite";

const points = [
  { name: "東京駅", lng: 139.767125, lat: 35.681236 },
  { name: "新宿駅", lng: 139.700258, lat: 35.690921 },
  { name: "渋谷駅", lng: 139.701636, lat: 35.658034 },
  { name: "浅草寺", lng: 139.796747, lat: 35.714765 },
  { name: "東京タワー", lng: 139.745438, lat: 35.658581 },
];

const map = new geolonia.maps.Map(document.getElementById("map"), {
  apiKey: "YOUR-API-KEY",
  center: { lat: 35.68, lng: 139.75 },
  zoom: 11,
});

for (const p of points) {
  new geolonia.maps.Marker({
    position: { lat: p.lat, lng: p.lng },
    map,
    title: p.name,
  });
}
```

- **`Marker({ position, map, title })`**: passing `map` attaches the marker to the map on the spot.
- To show a popup on click, combine `InfoWindow` and a click listener inside the loop.

### maps-react

`Marker` is an ordinary React component, so expanding the list with `map()` is all it takes.

```jsx
import "maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css";
import "@geolonia/maps-core/css";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import { Map, Marker } from "@geolonia/maps-react";

const points = [
  { name: "東京駅", lng: 139.767125, lat: 35.681236 },
  { name: "新宿駅", lng: 139.700258, lat: 35.690921 },
  { name: "渋谷駅", lng: 139.701636, lat: 35.658034 },
  { name: "浅草寺", lng: 139.796747, lat: 35.714765 },
  { name: "東京タワー", lng: 139.745438, lat: 35.658581 },
];

createRoot(document.getElementById("root")).render(
  <Map
    apiKey="YOUR-API-KEY"
    center={[139.75, 35.68]}
    zoom={11}
    containerStyle={{ width: "100%", height: "100vh" }}
  >
    {points.map((p) => (
      <Marker key={p.name} lat={p.lat} lng={p.lng}>
        {p.name}
      </Marker>
    ))}
  </Map>,
);
```

**When it does not work**

- Pins land in the sea: longitude and latitude are swapped. Check `lng` and `lat` in the list.
- Hundreds of points are slow or clump together: use clustering rather than markers.

---

## Switch the Map Style

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/howto/change-style/

Replace the base style of the map, meaning road colours, text sizes, building fills and so on.

### embed

Write a style name or a URL in the `data-style` attribute.

```html
<style>
  .geolonia { width: 100%; height: 100vh; }
</style>

<div class="geolonia"
     data-lat="35.68" data-lng="139.75" data-zoom="11"
     data-style="geolonia/gsi"></div>

<script src="https://cdn.geolonia.com/embed/v5/embed?geolonia-api-key=YOUR-API-KEY"></script>
```

- **`data-style`**: either a style name Geolonia provides, such as `geolonia/basic-v2`, `geolonia/midnight` or `geolonia/gsi`, or the URL of an external style JSON.
- Omitting it uses the Geolonia standard style.

Using an external URL:

```html
<div class="geolonia"
     data-lat="35.68" data-lng="139.75" data-zoom="11"
     data-style="https://tile.openstreetmap.jp/styles/osm-bright/style.json"></div>
```

### maps-suite

The initial style is given by the `style` option of `Map`. To switch at runtime, use `setStyle` on the underlying map.

```js
const map = new geolonia.maps.Map(document.getElementById("map"), {
  apiKey: "YOUR-API-KEY",
  center: { lat: 35.68, lng: 139.75 },
  zoom: 11,
  style: "geolonia/gsi",
});
```

```js
map.getGeoloniaMap().setStyle("https://tile.openstreetmap.jp/styles/osm-bright/style.json");
```

`setStyle` accepts either a style JSON URL or an inline style definition object.

### maps-react

Pass a style name or URL to the `style` prop of `Map`. Combined with state this builds a UI that **switches at runtime from a button**.

```jsx
import "maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css";
import "@geolonia/maps-core/css";
import { useState } from "react";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import { Map } from "@geolonia/maps-react";

function App() {
  const [style, setStyle] = useState("geolonia/basic-v2");
  return (
    <div style={{ display: "flex", flexDirection: "column", height: "100vh" }}>
      <div>
        <button onClick={() => setStyle("geolonia/basic-v2")}>標準</button>
        <button onClick={() => setStyle("geolonia/gsi")}>地理院</button>
      </div>
      <Map
        apiKey="YOUR-API-KEY"
        style={style}
        center={[139.75, 35.68]}
        zoom={11}
        containerStyle={{ flex: 1 }}
      />
    </div>
  );
}

createRoot(document.getElementById("root")).render(<App />);
```

- Passing the style as an **object**, an inline style definition, requires a stable reference such as a module constant. Creating a new object on every render reloads the style every time.

**When it does not work**

- The map turns blank white: check the spelling of the style name or URL. A style that does not exist renders nothing.
- An attribute has no effect: check the hyphens and spelling of `data-style`. Unknown attribute names are silently ignored.

---

## Show a Popup on Click

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/howto/popup-on-click/

### embed

HTML written inside the `.geolonia` div becomes the popup of the marker.

```html
<div class="geolonia"
     data-lat="35.681236" data-lng="139.767125"
     data-zoom="15">
  <strong>東京駅</strong><br>JR・地下鉄各線
</div>
```

- The child elements are the popup content. Being HTML, bold text, links and images all work.
- Writing children raises a marker at the centre, and clicking it opens the popup.
- An embed popup can be attached to **the single centre marker only**.

### maps-suite

Place a `Marker` and open an `InfoWindow` from the click event.

```js
const marker = new geolonia.maps.Marker({
  position: { lat: 35.681236, lng: 139.767125 },
  map,
  title: "東京駅",
});

const infoWindow = new geolonia.maps.InfoWindow({
  content: "<strong>東京駅</strong><br>JR・地下鉄各線",
});

marker.addListener("click", () => infoWindow.open(map, marker));
```

- **`InfoWindow`**: created with `content` as HTML, opened at the marker position by `open(map, marker)`. The arguments are **these two in this order**: map, then anchor.
- Creating several markers and attaching a listener to each gives individual popups on multiple points.

### maps-react

The **children** of the `Marker` component are the popup content.

```jsx
<Map
  apiKey="YOUR-API-KEY"
  center={[139.767125, 35.681236]}
  zoom={15}
  containerStyle={{ width: "100%", height: "100vh" }}
>
  <Marker lat={35.681236} lng={139.767125} color="#e4402f">
    <strong>東京駅</strong>
    <p style={{ margin: 0 }}>JR・地下鉄各線</p>
  </Marker>
</Map>
```

- **`lat` and `lng`**: separate props, unlike the `[longitude, latitude]` array of `center`.
- Unlike embed, several `Marker` elements can each carry **their own popup**.

**When it does not work**

- No marker appears: check that `data-marker="off"` is not present. Popups need a marker.
- The popup is empty: check that the children are not empty. Whitespace alone will not open one.
- Nothing happens on click: watch for an unclosed `div` tag.

---

## Load External GeoJSON Data

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/howto/geojson-data/

Overlay a GeoJSON file on the map to show your own points, lines and polygons.

### embed

Write the URL of the GeoJSON file in the `data-geojson` attribute.

```html
<div class="geolonia"
     data-lat="35.68" data-lng="139.75" data-zoom="11"
     data-marker="off"
     data-geojson="/data/sample-spots.geojson"></div>
```

- **`data-geojson`**: a path or URL. Either a path on the same server or an external URL that allows CORS.
- **`data-marker="off"`**: hides the default centre marker.

### maps-suite

Passing GeoJSON to `map.data` is the shortest form. Loading is awaited internally, so you do not have to wait yourself.

```js
const map = new geolonia.maps.Map(document.getElementById("map"), {
  apiKey: "YOUR-API-KEY",
  center: { lat: 35.68, lng: 139.75 },
  zoom: 11,
});

const res = await fetch("/data/sample-spots.geojson");
map.data.addGeoJson(await res.json());
```

`addGeoJson()` takes an object, so reading from a URL means going through `fetch`. Mixed points, lines and polygons can be passed as they are. Colours and line widths are set with something like `map.data.setStyle({ fillColor: "#f00", strokeWeight: 2 })`.

To control the drawing in detail, `map.data` only offers fill and stroke colour, opacity and width. Adjustments such as changing point size need `getGeoloniaMap()`, which touches the underlying maplibre map directly. **This is the escape hatch when you need something maps-suite does not provide.**

```js
await map.whenReady();
const impl = map.getGeoloniaMap();
impl.addSource("spots", { type: "geojson", data: "/data/sample-spots.geojson" });
impl.addLayer({
  id: "spots",
  type: "circle",
  source: "spots",
  paint: { "circle-radius": 8, "circle-color": "#e2543a" },
});
```

Here `whenReady()` waits for loading to complete, then `addSource` (data) is called before `addLayer` (drawing). The `data` passed to `addSource` may stay a URL.

### maps-react

Put `Source` (data) and `Layer` (drawing) as children of `Map`.

```jsx
<Map
  apiKey="YOUR-API-KEY"
  center={[139.75, 35.68]}
  zoom={11}
  containerStyle={{ width: "100%", height: "100vh" }}
>
  <Source id="spots" type="geojson" data="/data/sample-spots.geojson">
    <Layer id="spots" type="circle" />
  </Source>
</Map>
```

- **`<Layer>`**: **`id` is required.** Omitting it adds no layer and raises no error.

### The GeoJSON format

```json
{
  "type": "FeatureCollection",
  "features": [
    {
      "type": "Feature",
      "geometry": { "type": "Point", "coordinates": [139.767125, 35.681236] },
      "properties": { "name": "東京駅" }
    }
  ]
}
```

`coordinates` is in **`[longitude, latitude]`** order, the reverse of `data-lat` and `data-lng`.

**When it does not work**

- Points land in the sea: longitude and latitude are reversed in `coordinates`.
- Nothing appears: check the HTTP status of the file in the network tab. A 404 or a JSON syntax error is the usual cause.
- GeoJSON at an external URL will not load: a CORS restriction. Put the file on the same server or set CORS headers.

---

## Show the Current Location

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/howto/current-location/

Put a button on the map that, when pressed, takes the browser location and moves the map there.

### embed

Add `data-geolocate-control="on"`.

```html
<div class="geolonia"
     data-lat="35.68" data-lng="139.75" data-zoom="11"
     data-geolocate-control="on"></div>
```

A current-location button is added at the top right. Pressing it makes the browser ask for permission, and allowing it moves the map to that point.

### maps-suite

Take the location with the browser geolocation API, move with `setCenter` and raise a marker.

```js
navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition(
  (pos) => {
    const c = { lat: pos.coords.latitude, lng: pos.coords.longitude };
    map.setCenter(c);
    new geolonia.maps.Marker({ position: c, map, title: "現在地" });
  },
  (err) => console.warn("位置情報を取得できません", err),
);
```

- Use the second argument, the error callback, to prepare a fallback for refusal or failure, such as staying at the default place.

### maps-react

Add the `geolocateControl` prop.

```jsx
<Map
  apiKey="YOUR-API-KEY"
  center={[139.75, 35.68]}
  zoom={11}
  geolocateControl
  containerStyle={{ width: "100%", height: "100vh" }}
/>
```

**When it does not work**

- Pressing the button does nothing: check the browser location permission. If it is blocked, change it from the lock icon in the address bar.
- "Cannot get location": the geolocation API only works over HTTPS or on `localhost`. It is unavailable on `http://` sites.
- The location is off: GPS and network conditions introduce error. On desktop in particular the estimate is IP-based and can be far off.

---

## Fit All Points on Screen

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/howto/fit-bounds/

Rather than choosing `center` and `zoom` by hand, **compute the box enclosing every point and fit the map to it**. Everything stays visible even when the data changes.

### embed

Not available with HTML attributes alone. Switch to the maps-suite or maps-react code.

### maps-suite

```js
const points = [
  { lng: 139.767125, lat: 35.681236 },
  { lng: 139.700258, lat: 35.690921 },
  { lng: 139.701636, lat: 35.658034 },
  { lng: 139.796747, lat: 35.714765 },
  { lng: 139.745438, lat: 35.658581 },
];

for (const p of points) {
  new geolonia.maps.Marker({ position: p, map });
}

const north = Math.max(...points.map((p) => p.lat));
const south = Math.min(...points.map((p) => p.lat));
const east = Math.max(...points.map((p) => p.lng));
const west = Math.min(...points.map((p) => p.lng));

map.fitBounds({ north, south, east, west }, 40);
```

- **`fitBounds({ north, south, east, west }, padding)`**: fits the map to the given box. The second argument is the margin from the screen edge in pixels; without it the outermost points are cut off at the edge.
- `fitBounds()` waits for map load internally, so no wait is needed before calling it.

### maps-react

Receive the map instance in `onLoad` and call `fitBounds`.

```jsx
const handleLoad = (map) => {
  const north = Math.max(...points.map((p) => p.lat));
  const south = Math.min(...points.map((p) => p.lat));
  const east = Math.max(...points.map((p) => p.lng));
  const west = Math.min(...points.map((p) => p.lng));
  map.fitBounds([[west, south], [east, north]], { padding: 40 });
};

<Map
  apiKey="YOUR-API-KEY"
  center={[139.75, 35.68]}
  zoom={9}
  onLoad={handleLoad}
  containerStyle={{ width: "100%", height: "100vh" }}
>
  {points.map((p, i) => (
    <Marker key={i} lat={p.lat} lng={p.lng} />
  ))}
</Map>
```

- **`fitBounds`**: takes the box as `[[west, south], [east, north]]` here.

**When it does not work**

- Outer points are cut off: increase `padding`. Markers have pin height, so the top side needs particular margin.
- Only one point, or all points identical: the box has zero area and the map zooms in extremely far. With a single point, specifying `center` and `zoom` directly is simpler.

---

## Toggle Map Controls

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/howto/map-controls/

The buttons in the corners of the map, meaning zoom and rotation navigation, current location, fullscreen, scale and the Geolonia logo, can each be shown or hidden and positioned. Positions are one of `top-right`, `bottom-right`, `bottom-left` and `top-left`.

### embed

Each is set through a `data-*-control` attribute. Besides `on` and `off`, passing a position string also moves it.

```html
<div class="geolonia"
     data-lat="35.68" data-lng="139.75" data-zoom="11"
     data-navigation-control="on"
     data-geolocate-control="top-right"
     data-fullscreen-control="on"
     data-scale-control="bottom-left"></div>
```

- **`data-navigation-control`**: zoom and rotation buttons. Default `on`.
- **`data-geolocate-control`**: current-location button. Default `off`.
- **`data-fullscreen-control`**: fullscreen button. Default `off`.
- **`data-scale-control`**: scale bar. Default `off`.
- **`data-geolonia-control`**: position of the Geolonia logo. Default `bottom-left`.
- **`data-gesture-handling`**: default `on`. To avoid blocking page scrolling, it requires the `Ctrl` (or `alt`) key or two fingers to operate the map. Set it to `off` on pages where the map fills the view.

### maps-suite

The only control-related initialisation option is `disableDefaultUI`, which removes the default controls all at once. Adding controls individually or moving them means waiting for load and calling `addControl` on the underlying maplibre map.

With nothing specified, **navigation and the Geolonia logo are shown, while current location, fullscreen and scale are hidden**.

```js
const map = new geolonia.maps.Map(document.getElementById("map"), {
  apiKey: "YOUR-API-KEY",
  disableDefaultUI: true,
});
```

`disableDefaultUI` is all-or-nothing, so "keep only navigation" is not expressible. In that case remove everything and add back what you need.

```js
import maplibregl from "maplibre-gl";

await map.whenReady();
const impl = map.getGeoloniaMap();
impl.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl(), "top-right");
impl.addControl(new maplibregl.GeolocateControl({ trackUserLocation: true }), "top-right");
impl.addControl(new maplibregl.FullscreenControl(), "top-right");
impl.addControl(new maplibregl.ScaleControl(), "bottom-left");
```

- **`addControl(control, position)`**: omitting the second argument attaches at `top-right`.
- `NavigationControl` is present by default, so moving it means calling `removeControl` first and attaching it again.

### maps-react

Each is set through its own prop on `Map`. Besides `true` and `false`, a position string can be passed.

```jsx
<Map
  apiKey="YOUR-API-KEY"
  center={[139.75, 35.68]}
  zoom={11}
  navigationControl
  geolocateControl="top-right"
  fullscreenControl
  scaleControl="bottom-left"
  containerStyle={{ width: "100%", height: "100vh" }}
/>
```

The props are `navigationControl`, `geolocateControl`, `fullscreenControl`, `scaleControl` and `geoloniaControl`. Each takes `true` for the default position or a position string such as `"top-left"`.

**When it does not work**

- A control does not appear: check the spelling of the attribute or prop name. Wrong names are silently ignored.
- The current-location button does nothing: location works only over HTTPS or on `localhost`. Check the browser permission too.
- Scrolling over the map does not move it: `data-gesture-handling` is `on`. Set it to `off` on pages where the map fills the view.

---

## Switch the Map Language

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/howto/switch-language/

Labels such as place names can be shown in `ja` (Japanese), `en` (English) or `auto` (following the browser setting of the reader). The default is `auto`.

### embed

```html
<div class="geolonia"
     data-lat="35.68" data-lng="139.75" data-zoom="13"
     data-lang="en"></div>
```

- **`data-lang`**: one of `ja`, `en` and `auto`. Omitting it means `auto`.

### maps-suite

maps-suite has no language option in its initialisation, and the display language follows the browser setting, equivalent to `auto`. To pin the language explicitly, use embed or maps-react.

### maps-react

```jsx
<Map
  apiKey="YOUR-API-KEY"
  center={[139.75, 35.68]}
  zoom={13}
  lang="en"
  containerStyle={{ width: "100%", height: "100vh" }}
/>
```

- **`lang`**: one of `"ja"`, `"en"` and `"auto"`. Omitting it means `auto`.

Labels that have an English name are shown in English. Place names such as municipalities switch only where the style data carries an English name, and anything without one stays in the local script.

**When it does not work**

- The language does not change: label language depends on the data the style carries. In regions with no English place names the local script remains even when specified.
- Languages are mixed: the label for that feature is missing in the requested language. This is the intended behaviour, and the gaps are filled with the local script.

---

## Get Coordinates from a Draggable Marker

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/howto/draggable-marker/

Drag a marker and receive the latitude and longitude where it is released. Useful on screens for registering or editing a place, where the user drops the pin.

### embed

embed alone cannot make a draggable marker. Switch to the maps-suite or maps-react code.

### maps-suite

The maps-suite `Marker` does not support dragging, so wait for load and use the marker of the underlying maplibre map. `dragend` gives the position.

```js
import maplibregl from "maplibre-gl";

await map.whenReady();

const marker = new maplibregl.Marker({ draggable: true })
  .setLngLat([139.7671, 35.6812])
  .addTo(map.getGeoloniaMap());

marker.on("dragend", () => {
  const { lng, lat } = marker.getLngLat();
  console.log("緯度:", lat, "経度:", lng);
});
```

- **`new maplibregl.Marker({ draggable: true })`**: creates a marker with dragging enabled. `setLngLat` is in `[longitude, latitude]` order.
- **`marker.on("dragend", ...)`**: called once at the moment of release. Use `drag` to follow the movement itself.
- **`marker.getLngLat()`**: returns the current position, for writing back into latitude and longitude form fields.

### maps-react

Add `draggable` to `Marker` and receive the position in `onDragEnd`.

```jsx
function App() {
  const [pos, setPos] = useState({ lat: 35.6812, lng: 139.7671 });
  return (
    <div style={{ display: "flex", flexDirection: "column", height: "100vh" }}>
      <p>緯度: {pos.lat.toFixed(6)} / 経度: {pos.lng.toFixed(6)}</p>
      <Map
        apiKey="YOUR-API-KEY"
        center={[139.7671, 35.6812]}
        zoom={14}
        containerStyle={{ flex: 1 }}
      >
        <Marker
          lat={pos.lat}
          lng={pos.lng}
          draggable
          onDragEnd={(e) => {
            const { lng, lat } = e.target.getLngLat();
            setPos({ lat, lng });
          }}
        />
      </Map>
    </div>
  );
}
```

- **`onDragEnd`**: called when the drag is released. `e.target.getLngLat()` gives the release position.
- Keeping the coordinates in state makes them directly usable as form submission values.

**When it does not work**

- It will not drag: check that `draggable` is present, or `new maplibregl.Marker({ draggable: true })` in maps-suite.
- Confusion over `[longitude, latitude]`: `getLngLat()` returns a `{ lng, lat }` object. Converting to an array means `[longitude, latitude]` order.
- Coordinates do not update during the drag: `dragend` and `onDragEnd` fire on release only. Use `drag` or `onDrag` to follow the movement.

---

## Access the Map Instance Directly (maps-core)

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/howto/maps-core-access/

embed, maps-suite and maps-react all carry **the maps-core `GeoloniaMap`** underneath. `GeoloniaMap` extends the MapLibre GL JS `Map`, so once you have it, MapLibre GL JS APIs such as `on()`, `flyTo()` and `queryRenderedFeatures()` are available as they are. This is the escape hatch when what a library offers is not enough. Only the way you retrieve the instance differs per library.

### embed

Pass the target element to `geolonia.Map` and **create the map yourself**. What comes back is a `GeoloniaMap`.

```html
<!doctype html>
<html>
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <style>
      #map { width: 100%; height: 100vh; }
      #readout2 {
        position: absolute; top: 8px; left: 8px; z-index: 1;
        background: #fff; padding: 6px 10px; border-radius: 4px;
        font: 13px/1.5 system-ui, sans-serif;
      }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <div id="readout2">読み込み中</div>
    <div id="map" data-lat="35.68" data-lng="139.75" data-zoom="11"></div>

    <script src="https://cdn.geolonia.com/embed/v5/embed?geolonia-api-key=YOUR-API-KEY"></script>
    <script>
      const map = new geolonia.Map("#map");
      const readout = document.getElementById("readout2");

      map.on("load", () => {
        const show = () => {
          const c = map.getCenter();
          readout.textContent =
            `zoom ${map.getZoom().toFixed(2)} / ${c.lat.toFixed(4)}, ${c.lng.toFixed(4)}`;
        };
        map.on("move", show);
        show();
      });
    </script>
  </body>
</html>
```

- There is no `class="geolonia"` here. embed only creates maps automatically on elements carrying `.geolonia`, so the class is removed and the element is passed by `id`.
- Attributes such as `data-lat` are still read when you create the map yourself. Anything expressible as an attribute stays usable, with no need to rewrite it in JavaScript.
- Waiting for `map.on("load", ...)` means touching the map only after the style has loaded.

**Calling it on an element that already has a map returns the existing instance rather than creating a new one.** Calling `new geolonia.Map(".geolonia")` while `class="geolonia"` is still present will not produce two maps. This is also how you reach a map that embed created automatically.

The `geoloniaMap` property of the element also gives it, but that one is **`undefined` until the map has been created**. embed creates the map when the element enters the viewport, so a map off screen does not exist until it is scrolled into view. `new geolonia.Map()` either creates it there and then or returns the existing one, so timing does not matter.

Loading embed also puts the contents of MapLibre GL JS on `window.geolonia`, so MapLibre classes such as `new geolonia.Popup()` are usable directly.

### maps-suite

`map.getGeoloniaMap()` returns the underlying `GeoloniaMap`. Call it after waiting for load.

```js
const map = new geolonia.maps.Map(container, {
  apiKey: "YOUR-API-KEY",
  center: { lat: 35.68, lng: 139.75 },
  zoom: 11,
});

await map.whenReady();
const impl = map.getGeoloniaMap();

const show = () => {
  const c = impl.getCenter();
  readout.textContent =
    `zoom ${impl.getZoom().toFixed(2)} / ${c.lat.toFixed(4)}, ${c.lng.toFixed(4)}`;
};
impl.on("move", show);
show();
```

The maps-suite `Map` has `getZoom()` and `getCenter()` of its own, so this particular example does not need to descend to the underlying map. The real use is for **things maps-suite does not offer**, such as adding sources and layers, changing the projection, or attaching and detaching controls.

`whenReady()` is awaited because touching layers before the style has loaded raises an error. Read-only calls such as `getCenter()` work without waiting, but keeping it uniform is safer.

Note that `getMap()` is a different thing. Overlays such as `Marker`, `Polyline` and `Circle` have `getMap()`, but it returns **the maps-suite `Map` the overlay sits on**, not the underlying `GeoloniaMap`. To descend all the way, call `getGeoloniaMap()` on the returned `Map`.

```js
marker.getMap().getGeoloniaMap();
```

### maps-react

The `ref` of `Map` is the `GeoloniaMap` itself. However, **the map is created after mount**, so receiving it with `useRef` and reading it in `useEffect` finds `null`. To act the moment the instance exists, **pass a function as `ref`**, a callback ref, which React calls with the instance when it connects the element.

```jsx
function App() {
  const [text, setText] = useState("読み込み中");

  const mapRef = useCallback((map) => {
    if (!map) return;

    const show = () => {
      const c = map.getCenter();
      setText(
        `zoom ${map.getZoom().toFixed(2)} / ${c.lat.toFixed(4)}, ${c.lng.toFixed(4)}`,
      );
    };

    map.on("move", show);
    show();

    return () => {
      map.off("move", show);
    };
  }, []);

  return (
    <Map
      ref={mapRef}
      apiKey="YOUR-API-KEY"
      center={[139.75, 35.68]}
      zoom={11}
      containerStyle={{ width: "100%", height: "100%" }}
    />
  );
}
```

**Cleanup can be written as the return value.** The example detaches the listener with `off("move", show)` inside the returned function.

Returning a cleanup function from a callback ref requires **React 19 or later**. On 18 and earlier the return value is ignored, and instead the callback is called again with `null` when the element detaches. On 18, subscribe when `map` arrives and unsubscribe when called with `null`.

To touch the map at arbitrary times later, keep the received instance yourself.

```jsx
const mapRef = useRef(null);

<Map
  ref={(map) => { mapRef.current = map; }}
  apiKey="YOUR-API-KEY"
  center={[139.75, 35.68]}
  zoom={11}
/>

<button onClick={() => mapRef.current?.flyTo({ center: [135.5, 34.7], zoom: 12 })}>
  大阪へ
</button>
```

The `ref` fires right after the map is created and **does not wait for the style to load**. Adding layers and sources before load raises an error, so check `isStyleLoaded()` and wait with `once("load")` if it is not ready.

```jsx
const mapRef = useCallback((map) => {
  if (!map) return;

  const addLayer = () => {
    map.addSource("spots", { type: "geojson", data: "/data/sample-spots.geojson" });
    map.addLayer({ id: "spots", type: "circle", source: "spots" });
  };

  if (map.isStyleLoaded()) addLayer();
  else map.once("load", addLayer);
}, []);
```

`Map` also has an `onLoad` prop, which hands over the `GeoloniaMap` after loading completes. It is shorter for one-off initialisation, but **there is nowhere to detach listeners**, so use a callback ref if you subscribe with `on()`.

Anything expressible the React way is available through props. `onMove` covers following map movement, and `<Source>` and `<Layer>` cover drawing data. Touching the underlying instance is for **operations with no prop**.

**When it does not work**

- embed `geoloniaMap` is `undefined`: the map has not been created yet. embed creates it when the element enters the viewport. Retrieve it with `new geolonia.Map()` instead.
- embed reports "No HTML elements found matching": no element matches the selector passed. This also happens when the script is placed before the element.
- "Style is not done loading": layers are being touched before the style has loaded. Await `whenReady()` in maps-suite, or check `isStyleLoaded()` and wait with `once("load")` in maps-react.
- maps-react gave `null` with `useRef` plus `useEffect`: the map is created after mount, so it is not there on the first effect. Pass a function as `ref`.
- Operations on the retrieved instance have no effect: changing values maps-suite manages, meaning centre, zoom, tilt and heading, from the underlying side has undefined behaviour. Change those through maps-suite methods.

The full set of what the retrieved instance can do is everything the MapLibre GL JS `Map` can do; see https://maplibre.org/maplibre-gl-js/docs/API/classes/Map/. What Geolonia adds is in https://docs.geolonia.com/reference/core/.

---

## Cluster a Large Number of Points

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/howto/clustering/

Hundreds or thousands of points on a map overlap and become hard to read. Clustering groups nearby points automatically, shows a count label, and splits them into individual points as you zoom in.

### embed

Add `data-cluster="on"`.

```html
<div class="geolonia"
     data-lat="35.67" data-lng="139.74" data-zoom="10"
     data-marker="off"
     data-geojson="/data/dense-points.geojson"
     data-cluster="on"></div>
```

- **`data-cluster="on"`**: clusters the GeoJSON points automatically.
- **`data-cluster-color`**: changes the cluster colour, for example `data-cluster-color="#e74c3c"`.

### maps-suite

Passing an array of markers to `MarkerClusterer` groups nearby points automatically.

```js
const res = await fetch("/data/dense-points.geojson");
const gj = await res.json();

const markers = gj.features.map(
  (f) =>
    new geolonia.maps.Marker({
      position: { lng: f.geometry.coordinates[0], lat: f.geometry.coordinates[1] },
    }),
);

new geolonia.maps.MarkerClusterer({ map, markers });
```

- Create the `Marker` objects **without passing `map`**, leaving them detached. `MarkerClusterer` manages attaching them.
- **`MarkerClusterer({ map, markers })`**: groups nearby markers into counted clusters that split on zoom.

### maps-react

Adding `cluster` to `Source` makes maplibre build the clusters. You decide the drawing, so three layers are needed: **the cluster circles, the count labels, and the points that did not cluster**.

```jsx
<Source
  id="spots"
  type="geojson"
  data="/data/dense-points.geojson"
  cluster
  clusterRadius={50}
>
  <Layer
    id="clusters"
    type="circle"
    filter={["has", "point_count"]}
    paint={{
      "circle-color": "#e2543a",
      "circle-radius": ["step", ["get", "point_count"], 16, 10, 22, 50, 30],
      "circle-opacity": 0.85,
    }}
  />
  <Layer
    id="cluster-count"
    type="symbol"
    filter={["has", "point_count"]}
    layout={{
      "text-field": ["get", "point_count_abbreviated"],
      "text-font": ["Noto Sans Regular"],
      "text-size": 12,
    }}
    paint={{ "text-color": "#ffffff" }}
  />
  <Layer
    id="unclustered"
    type="circle"
    filter={["!", ["has", "point_count"]]}
    paint={{
      "circle-color": "#e2543a",
      "circle-radius": 6,
      "circle-stroke-width": 1.5,
      "circle-stroke-color": "#ffffff",
    }}
  />
</Source>
```

- **`cluster`**: `Source` takes the maplibre source definition as it is, so `cluster` and `clusterRadius`, the grouping distance in pixels, work directly.
- **`filter`**: features carrying `point_count` are clusters, those without are single points. The two are drawn by separate layers.
- **`point_count_abbreviated`**: the count in short form, turning `1200` into something like `1.2k`.
- **`text-font`**: name a font included in the Geolonia style. The maplibre default font name is not included, so omitting this shows no counts.

**When it does not work**

- Nothing clusters: check that `data-cluster="on"` is written. The value is `"on"`, not `"true"`.
- Nothing appears: check the `data-geojson` path. The file must exist on the server and be reachable.

---

## Colour Areas by Value (Choropleth)

URL: https://docs.geolonia.com/howto/choropleth/

A map showing numbers such as population or sales through the shading of areas (polygons) is called a **choropleth**. Give the polygon GeoJSON a numeric property and write the value-to-colour mapping as an expression.

### Preparing the data

```json
{
  "type": "Feature",
  "geometry": { "type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [ ... ] },
  "properties": { "name": "エリアA", "value": 72 }
}
```

### embed

Not available with HTML attributes alone. Switch to the maps-suite or maps-react code.

### maps-suite

Wait for load, then stack a `fill` layer whose `fill-color` carries an `interpolate` expression.

```js
await map.whenReady();
const impl = map.getGeoloniaMap();
impl.addSource("areas", { type: "geojson", data: "/data/areas.geojson" });
impl.addLayer({
  id: "areas",
  type: "fill",
  source: "areas",
  paint: {
    "fill-color": [
      "interpolate", ["linear"], ["get", "value"],
      0, "#ffffcc",
      50, "#fd8d3c",
```
